questions.q: What is Avana?
questions.a:
Avana lets liquidity providers use AMM positions as collateral on Aave V4. A borrower pledges a Uniswap v3 position on Ethereum or an Aerodrome Slipstream position on Base. Avana's LPVault holds the position, and a matching vault token is supplied as collateral on an Avana CDP Spoke. The borrower then borrows GHO, or another debt asset the Spoke lends, while the liquidity stays in the pool.

Avana launches on Ethereum and Base, with an Avana Stable LP Hub on each chain. The Hubs and Spokes are standard, unmodified Aave V4 contracts owned and configured by the Aave DAO. Avana's own contracts handle custody, valuation, borrower actions and liquidation.

questions.q: What problem does Avana solve?
questions.a:
Liquidity providers usually have to remove liquidity before they can borrow against it. That means leaving the pool and giving up fee income and their chosen range.

Avana makes supported LP positions usable as collateral while they stay in the pool. The LPOracle values each position from its token amounts at oracle prices, and Aave V4 records it as a vault token. The benefit to LPs is capital flexibility, not a guaranteed return. Borrowers still bear impermanent loss, price risk and liquidation risk.

questions.q: How is Avana different from a standard lending market?
questions.a:
Standard lending markets treat collateral as token balances. An LP position holds several tokens, earns fees, shifts composition as prices move, can move out of range, and needs a specific route to unwind.

Avana therefore sets risk per market. A market is one pool and one exact tick range on one CDP Spoke, with its own vault token, Collateral Factor, caps, price route and swap routes. Each wallet has a separate account for each market, so one market's collateral never backs debt in another.

questions.q: Which AMMs does Avana support?
questions.a:
At launch, Avana supports Uniswap v3 positions on Ethereum and Aerodrome Slipstream positions on Base. Slipstream positions must be unstaked; a gauge-staked position cannot be pledged. Each market accepts one exact tick range, and a position with any other range is refused.

Avana's core is AMM-neutral. Integrations for Uniswap v2, Curve StableSwap-NG, Balancer and Uniswap v4 are specified, but each is listed only after its readiness checks pass and governance approves it. Pools with fee-on-transfer, rebasing or hook tokens are excluded.

questions.q: Does Avana replace the AMM where my liquidity sits?
questions.a:
No. The AMM still handles swaps, pool state, price movement and fee generation. Avana adds a collateral layer around supported positions.

When you pledge a position, the LPVault for that AMM holds the NFT, and Avana mints vault tokens equal to the position's liquidity. The liquidity stays in the pool and keeps earning fees while it is in range. You can collect those fees at any time.

questions.q: Is Avana deployed?
questions.a:
Not yet. The Avana specification and contract interfaces are complete and have been through internal review and formal modelling. The contract code is written next, followed by independent audits of every contract and the Aave DAO votes that approve deployment and funding.

Contract addresses will be listed on the Contracts page of the developer docs once the contracts are deployed. The public sandbox at app.avana.cc uses simulated assets.

questions.q: How does Avana work at a high level?
questions.a:
You pledge a supported position through the AaveAdapter. The LPVault takes custody of the NFT, Collateralization records how much liquidity it backs, and the AaveAdapter mints that many vault tokens to your PositionProxy for the market. The proxy supplies them as collateral on the market's CDP Spoke. You then borrow through the AaveAdapter, which checks prices, caps and your health factor.

Repayment, withdrawal, partial liquidity removal, repay with collateral and fee collection also run through the AaveAdapter. Liquidation runs through LPVaultSwap. Every upgrade or parameter change to Avana's contracts goes through the chain's AvanaTimelock.

questions.q: Why does Avana use Aave V4 Hubs and Spokes?
questions.a:
Aave V4 separates shared liquidity (Hubs) from market-specific risk settings (Spokes). Each chain has an Avana Stable LP Hub. The Aave DAO supplies a capped GHO credit line to it through a supply-only Lend Spoke, and only Avana's CDP Spokes can draw from it.

There is one CDP Spoke per chain, Hub, AMM protocol and risk tier. At launch these are "Uniswap v3 Stable" on Ethereum and "Aerodrome Slipstream Stable" on Base. Correlated LP and Volatile LP Hubs are designed for later. Avana does not fork or modify Aave V4.

questions.q: What is a CDP Spoke?
questions.a:
A CDP Spoke is a standard Aave V4 Spoke owned by the Aave DAO. It holds one collateral-only vault-token reserve per Avana market and the debt reserves enabled for it, GHO first. It applies each market's Collateral Factor, liquidation bonus and caps.

Every vault-token reserve uses three required settings: receiving shares is disabled, the Aave liquidation fee is 0 (or paid to Avana's fee recipient), and no reinvestment controller is set. Together with the vault token's transfer rule, these make LPVaultSwap the only contract that can receive seized collateral.

questions.q: What are Avana vault tokens?
questions.a:
Vault tokens are collateral-only ERC-20 tokens, one per market. One base unit equals one unit of credited liquidity. Decimals are fixed per market between 6 and 18 at listing. Only the AaveAdapter mints and burns them, and they move only between registered PositionProxies, the CDP Spoke and LPVaultSwap.

Vault tokens have no secondary market, no emissions and no exchange rate. Their supply never exceeds the liquidity Collateralization has credited plus any units awaiting settlement.

questions.q: What are the main parts of the Avana protocol?
questions.a:
Custody: an immutable LPVault per AMM protocol per chain, and the Collateralization ledger. Accounts and tokens: VaultToken and VaultTokenFactory, PositionProxy and ProxyManager. Policy: the AaveAdapter (borrower entry point), RiskModule (checks), MarketRegistry (markets, routes, pause state, breakers) and ParameterStore (risk parameters).

Oracles: an LPOracle per market and a DebtOracle per non-GHO debt asset. Liquidation: LPVaultSwap, swap-route contracts and the PayoutEscrow, plus Avana's public flash liquidation helper for callers that hold none of the debt asset. Repay with collateral uses a flash source over the Aave V3 Pool. Infrastructure: AvanaTimelock, Lock and the read-only Lens. The Developers section lists every contract on its Contracts page.

questions.q: What happens when I deposit LP collateral?
questions.a:
You approve the LPVault for your position's NFT and call pledge on the AaveAdapter. The LPVault checks that the position matches the market's pool and exact range and takes custody. The RiskModule checks the price state, the market's status, the minimum pledge ($10 at launch), the market, token and depositor caps, the pool-share limit, the 16-record limit per account and market, and any breakers.

If the checks pass, the AaveAdapter deploys your PositionProxy for the market if needed, mints vault tokens equal to the credited liquidity and supplies them as collateral. Pledging does not borrow anything. There is no allowlist and no maximum position size beyond the caps.

questions.q: Does my LP position stay active after deposit?
questions.a:
Yes. Pledging changes custody but does not remove liquidity. The pool keeps processing swaps and your position keeps earning fees. A concentrated position stops earning fees while it is out of range.

You can add liquidity to a pledged NFT and credit it with recredit, remove part of the liquidity while keeping the NFT pledged with removeLiquidity, or top up with another position in the same market.

questions.q: Can I claim LP fees while borrowing?
questions.a:
Yes. The depositor can call collectFees on the AaveAdapter at any time. The AMM pays the fees directly to you. Collecting fees does not change your vault tokens, caps, debt or health factor.

No pause, freeze, breaker or price state blocks fee collection. On Base it also works during a sequencer outage through L1 forced inclusion.

questions.q: Are LP fees included in collateral value?
questions.a:
No. The LPOracle values only the liquidity behind each vault token. Uncollected fees are excluded from the price, and a liquidation never seizes them.

Borrowing limits come from the market's Collateral Factor, applied separately. The oracle value itself has no haircut.

questions.q: When can I withdraw LP collateral?
questions.a:
With no debt, you can withdraw at any time, and no pause, freeze, breaker or price state blocks it. repayAllAndWithdraw repays every debt and returns the position in one call.

With debt, a withdrawal needs the Hub not to be paused (a frozen Hub still allows it), your address not to be frozen, Live prices, an up sequencer on Base, no tripped breaker, and a health factor at or above your chosen minimum afterwards. The LPVault returns the NFT with its uncollected fees.

questions.q: How many positions can one account hold?
questions.a:
Each wallet has one PositionProxy, and so one Aave account, per CDP Spoke and market. An account holds at most 16 backing records for its market. A position in another market opens a separate account with its own health factor.

If an account is liquidated, Collateralization seizes its records largest first.

questions.q: How does Avana price LP collateral?
questions.a:
The LPOracle prices each vault token by fair composition: it works out the token amounts behind one unit of liquidity at the oracle price ratio, clamped to the market's range, and multiplies them by Chainlink USD prices. Amounts are rounded down and uncollected fees are excluded. Prices have 8 decimals, and the oracle never reverts and never returns 0.

GHO debt is priced at a fixed $1. Other debt assets are priced by their own DebtOracle.

questions.q: How does Avana handle oracle failures?
questions.a:
Each token has a primary and an alternate Chainlink route and a pre-approved standby route. Prices must be fresh within the feed's heartbeat plus a margin. Borrowing also needs an independent second source to agree, a pool TWAP consistency check, and stablecoins within a $0.90–$1.02 band.

Each market's price is in one of four states: Live, Drifting, Cached or Expired. Cached (up to 1 hour) and Expired block new borrowing and liquidation of that market. Expired values the collateral at almost zero while repayment and debt-free exits continue. After recovery, a 30-minute grace period allows liquidation only below a health factor of 0.95.

questions.q: Does Avana discount the oracle value?
questions.a:
No. The oracle reports value with no haircut. Each market's Collateral Factor sets how much of that value can support debt: the lowest Aave V4 Collateral Factor among the pool's tokens multiplied by a pool risk factor of at most 40%. A GHO leg uses an explicit factor set at listing.

Gauntlet's analysis of LP collateral recommends conservative starting factors, as low as 0.25× the lower underlying factor when the borrowed asset is not one of the pool's tokens. Final factors are calibrated per market with Aave's service providers.

questions.q: Why are concentrated liquidity positions treated carefully?
questions.a:
A concentrated position changes composition quickly as price moves and can move out of range. Avana therefore lists each exact range as its own market, values it with the range clamped, and sets a pool risk factor for it.

The LPVault refuses a position whose range differs from the market's, and the LPOracle checks pool state against a TWAP before borrowing.

questions.q: What market data does Avana monitor?
questions.a:
Avana's keeper and monitoring track price states, pool share, pool depth, seizures, swap-route failures, deficits and the Aave configuration of every reserve. Some conditions trip on-chain breakers; others raise alerts, such as a 3% price drop in 2 hours, more than 20% of a market seized in 1 hour, 3 swap-route failures in 1 hour, or Avana holding more than 25% of a pool.

Avana Labs publishes weekly usage reports and monthly revenue reports covering debt and collateral by market, concentration, health factors, liquidations, Avana Umbrella usage, bad debt, oracle incidents, pauses and breaker trips, credit-line usage and fees.

questions.q: How does borrowing work on Avana?
questions.a:
You call borrow on the AaveAdapter with the market, the debt reserve, the amount, a deadline, the minimum health factor you accept and your expected nonce. The RiskModule checks Live prices, debt-price freshness, breakers, the pause state and that at least one committed operator is active on the chain. Your PositionProxy borrows on the CDP Spoke and the funds are sent to you.

Interest accrues at the Hub base rate × (1 + your risk premium), so your health factor can change even if your collateral does not.

questions.q: How is borrowing capacity calculated?
questions.a:
Borrowing capacity = LP position value × LP Collateral Factor, and LP Collateral Factor = lowest token Collateral Factor × pool risk factor. Capacity also depends on existing debt, caps, the credit line's available liquidity and oracle checks.

Example values: a USDC/USDT Slipstream position worth $20,000 with a Collateral Factor of 31.20% gives $6,240 of weighted collateral. The Lens recommends borrowing up to a health factor of 1.10 (5,673.29 USDC here) and shows the maximum at 1.00 (6,209.56 USDC).

questions.q: Why is borrow power lower than my LP value?
questions.a:
The Collateral Factor leaves room for price moves, impermanent loss, range changes and liquidation costs. The pool risk factor is capped at 40%, so with two tokens at 78% the opening loan-to-value is at most about 28.4%.

The gap between value and capacity differs between markets because each market has its own pool risk factor.

questions.q: What assets can I borrow?
questions.a:
GHO is the first debt asset on every CDP Spoke. Other assets, such as USDC, USDT or WETH, can be enabled as debt reserves on a CDP Spoke through governance, each funded by its own credit line and priced by its own DebtOracle.

At launch the credit line is GHO from the Aave DAO: 2M GHO proposed on Ethereum, with the Base line set in the funding proposal.

questions.q: Can I borrow against multiple LP positions at once?
questions.a:
Within one market, yes: up to 16 positions back one account and one health factor. Positions in different markets are separate accounts, each with its own health factor, so they do not back each other.

Within an account you can borrow more than one debt asset if the CDP Spoke lends them.

questions.q: Is there a minimum health factor for borrowing?
questions.a:
On-chain, the only limit is Aave's health factor of 1.00. The borrow call takes your own minimum health factor and reverts below it. The Lens recommends staying at or above 1.10.

There is no minimum debt. A per-market hard health floor exists but is off at launch.

questions.q: Who supplies the liquidity Avana borrowers use?
questions.a:
At launch, the Aave DAO treasury supplies a capped GHO credit line to each chain's Avana Stable LP Hub through a supply-only Lend Spoke. Public deposits are not open at launch.

Each CDP Spoke's draw cap on an asset is set by the Aave DAO, and the draw caps sum to at most the credit line.

questions.q: Where does supplier yield come from?
questions.a:
Borrowers pay the Hub's base rate plus their risk premium. The Avana Hub's GHO rate is flat, independent of utilization, and set by the Aave DAO at or above the Core Hub GHO base rate.

All interest on Aave DAO-funded credit lines goes to the Aave DAO. Avana charges no fee on borrow interest.

questions.q: Do suppliers manage LP collateral themselves?
questions.a: No. Suppliers do not choose ranges or handle settlement. The CDP Spokes, Avana's custody contracts and LPVaultSwap handle valuation, health checks and liquidation.

questions.q: What protects lender capital?
questions.a:
Per-market Collateral Factors with a pool risk factor of at most 40%, market, token and depositor caps per Hub, oracle states and breakers, liquidation open to any address alongside Avana's keeper, and draw caps that stay within the chain's flash liquidity so every borrow can be liquidated in one transaction.

If a liquidation leaves debt without collateral, the deficit is covered by the Avana Umbrella for that Hub and asset, a first-loss reserve funded by Avana Labs and controlled by the Aave DAO, within 72 hours. A deficit larger than the reserve is a loss to that Hub asset's suppliers, realized by the Aave DAO.

questions.q: What is the health factor?
questions.a:
Health factor = collateral value × Collateral Factor ÷ debt value, computed by Aave per account, which means per market. Below 1, the account can be liquidated.

Example values: $6,240 of weighted collateral against 4,999.50 USDC of debt gives a health factor of 1.2481.

questions.q: What affects my health factor?
questions.a:
Collateral prices, the composition of the position within its range, interest on your debt, debt-asset prices, and governance changes to the Collateral Factor. During a market's offboarding, its liquidation threshold falls once a day for 30 days.

Repaying, topping up or repaying with collateral raises it. Borrowing, withdrawing or removing liquidity lowers it.

questions.q: How does liquidation work on Avana?
questions.a:
When an account's health factor is below 1, any address can call liquidate on LPVaultSwap. In one transaction LPVaultSwap takes the debt asset from the caller, calls Aave's liquidationCall to repay part of the debt and receive vault tokens plus the bonus, unwinds the matching liquidity and swaps the tokens into the debt asset on fixed routes. A caller without the debt asset can use Avana's public flash liquidation helper, which flash-borrows it from the chain's Aave V3 Pool and repays the loan from the caller's payout.

Every liquidation is partial and sized by Aave's rules. The recovered amount must reach an oracle-derived floor. Avana's fee and any borrower surplus are paid first; the caller receives the rest: its unused funding, the recovered principal and its reward, paid directly or the liquidation reverts.

questions.q: Who can liquidate an unhealthy position?
questions.a:
Any address that is not frozen can call liquidate, LPVaultSwap's only liquidation entry point, with either the primary-then-backup or the backup-only swap routes. The caller funds the debt asset itself or through Avana's public flash liquidation helper, and pays any shortfall below the recovery floor up to a limit it sets. Avana's keeper is the committed operator on each chain: it commits to liquidate every account below a health factor of 1, but registration gives it no power any other caller lacks.

Anyone can also call settlePending to settle vault tokens left by an unfinished seizure; the proceeds go to the Avana Umbrella and the caller receives nothing.

questions.q: What fees apply during liquidation?
questions.a:
Avana's fee is 20% of the oracle gain (the seized collateral's value at oracle prices minus the debt repaid), limited to what the liquidation actually realizes. The liquidator receives the rest of the oracle gain. Recovery above oracle value goes to the borrower. A liquidator that borrows through the flash liquidation helper pays any flash premium from its own payout.

Your uncollected LP fees are never taken. Repay with collateral pays no bonus and no Avana fee, only the flash premium.

questions.q: What can stop a liquidation?
questions.a:
Pauses, freezes and breakers never stop liquidation. A liquidation does need a usable price: Cached or Expired prices block it, and for 30 minutes after a price recovery or a Base sequencer restart, only accounts below a health factor of 0.95 can be liquidated.

A liquidation also reverts if the swap routes cannot reach the recovery floor and the caller does not cover the shortfall. An Aave-side reserve pause can block it too.

questions.q: How are new LP markets added?
questions.a:
Avana Labs proposes markets and parameters for assessment by a designated risk reviewer. Each market is listed through the chain's AvanaTimelock at the normal delay, a five-day public review enforced on-chain, together with the Aave DAO's listing payload for the Collateral Factor, bonus and caps.

A pool needs reliable external pricing, enough liquidity history, routes that can recover liquidation proceeds under stress, and no restrictions on removing liquidity.

questions.q: Can risk parameters change over time?
questions.a:
Yes, through the AvanaTimelock. Changes that loosen risk wait the normal 5-day delay and are bounded: a USD cap can rise by at most 50% and a slippage allowance by at most 25 bps per delay. Changes that only reduce risk can use the 12-hour short delay.

The Emergency Guardian and the Aave Protocol Guardian can pause or freeze a Hub, freeze an address, trip a breaker or switch to a standby price route at once, but cannot upgrade contracts, change parameters or move funds. The Aave DAO can also freeze or pause Avana reserves on the Aave side.

questions.q: Where can I follow governance discussion?
questions.a:
Avana is discussed on the Aave governance forum (governance.aave.com). The ARFC goes to a Snapshot vote, followed by a deployment ARFC and a funding ARFC, then AIPs.

Avana Labs also posts updates on X at https://twitter.com/avana_labs.

questions.q: How does Avana Labs earn revenue?
questions.a:
Avana Labs earns 20% of the oracle gain on each liquidation, set by avanaFeeShareBps and changed only through the timelock, and an app fee charged by its app outside the contracts. No contract computes or enforces the app fee, so calling the contracts directly does not pay it.

Avana charges no fee on borrow interest. Interest on the Aave DAO's credit lines goes to the DAO.

questions.q: Can I borrow GHO through Avana?
questions.a:
Yes. GHO is the first debt asset on every CDP Spoke, funded by the Aave DAO's capped credit line to the Avana Stable LP Hub. GHO debt is priced at a fixed $1.

GHO debt accrues interest at the Hub's GHO rate plus your risk premium. All of that interest goes to the Aave DAO.

questions.q: Can GHO be part of LP collateral?
questions.a: Yes. A stablecoin pool that contains GHO can be listed. Its GHO leg uses an explicit Collateral Factor set at listing instead of an Aave V4 Core Hub factor.

questions.q: How do I repay GHO debt?
questions.a:
Call repay on the AaveAdapter, or have anyone repay on your behalf. Set repayAll to repay the full debt at inclusion; any unused amount up to your spend cap is returned. No Avana pause, breaker, freeze, price or sequencer state blocks repayment; only an Aave-side reserve pause can.

You can also repay with collateral: LPVaultSwap flash-borrows the debt asset, repays it, unwinds part of your position and swaps it to cover the loan. After full repayment, you can withdraw the position.

questions.q: What is Avana Multiply?
questions.a:
Multiply is a flow in Avana's public sandbox at app.avana.cc. In one workflow, it borrows against LP collateral and reinvests the borrowed funds to increase exposure. The sandbox uses simulated assets and makes no onchain transactions.

Multiply is not part of Avana's Aave V4 markets, which cover borrowing against Uniswap v3 positions on Ethereum and Aerodrome Slipstream positions on Base.

questions.q: How is Multiply different from borrowing?
questions.a:
Borrowing gives you assets you can use directly while the account stays healthy. Multiply uses LP-backed borrowing power inside a managed strategy. The borrowed capital goes into approved exposure and is tracked as one position.

Multiply adds leverage. Leverage increases capital efficiency and potential returns, but it also increases downside, liquidation risk, and sensitivity to price movement. The health view matters more, not less, when a position is looped.

questions.q: Do I keep my LP while using Multiply?
questions.a:
Yes. The LP position remains the collateral base while the Multiply position is open. You do not need to exit the AMM position to create leveraged exposure.

The LP position still backs debt, so collateral rules apply, and it can be liquidated if the account becomes unhealthy. Users monitor collateral value, debt, leverage, and liquidation buffer for as long as the loop is open.

questions.q: What limits maximum leverage?
questions.a:
Maximum leverage depends on collateral quality, pool liquidity, volatility, oracle confidence, borrow asset, market caps, and liquidation assumptions. Stable or highly correlated pools usually support different leverage limits than volatile or thin pools.

Avana uses market-specific risk controls. Leverage is limited by the actual LP collateral behind the position, not by a flat multiplier applied to every pool.

questions.q: Can automation help manage position risk?
questions.a:
The sandbox previews automation that monitors account health and triggers actions such as repayment or deleveraging before liquidation. Automation is not part of Avana's Aave V4 markets, but repay and repay with collateral can be called by any service you authorize to send the transaction.

Automation is a risk-management tool, not a guarantee. Market moves, liquidity conditions, transaction delays, oracle updates, and route availability can still affect execution.

questions.q: Can LP collateral support perps-style exposure?
questions.a:
No. Avana covers borrowing against approved Uniswap v3 positions on Ethereum and Aerodrome Slipstream positions on Base.

You decide how to use the assets you borrow, but Avana does not route LP-backed credit into perps or other strategies.

questions.q: What do users monitor after opening a position?
questions.a:
Borrowers monitor health factor, debt, collateral value, borrowing rate, range status, the market's price state and distance to liquidation. The Lens exposes these values, including recommended and maximum borrow amounts and cap headroom.

In the sandbox Multiply flow, users also see leverage level and unwind controls.
